payload.rationale: Miami visits San Francisco in Week 2 of the 2026 season. Supplied facts: Miami is 0-1 after a 13-27 loss; San Francisco is 1-0 after a 27-7 win. Injury report shows Miami missing two linebackers (Chop Robinson notably), while the 49ers' listed absences are minor (a depth WR out; RB and K questionable). Background: the 49ers have been a structurally stronger franchise with a top-tier offensive scheme and roster core, playing at home where NFL home advantage is worth roughly 2-2.5 points; Miami entered 2026 with more roster and quarterback uncertainty and has historically struggled on the road against strong NFC opponents. Combining a prior that San Francisco is the better team, home-field advantage, and the (small-sample) Week 1 point differentials, a road Miami win looks like roughly a 30% proposition. Reasons this could be too high: if the 49ers are healthy and Miami's Week 1 loss reflects genuine decline (or Miami's QB situation is poor), the true probability could be closer to 22-25%. Reasons this could be too low: one-game samples are noisy, Miami's offense has recently had explosive upside, unknown 49ers injuries (e.g., to key skill players or QB) are not reflected in this packet, and NFL single-game outcomes are inherently high-variance; a near coin-flip is possible if the teams are closer than assumed. Ties are excluded from scoring.
limitations: Only Week 1 results available; very small sample and no opponent adjustment.
Final inactive lists and possible late injuries are unknown.
No fitted power-rating model; estimate relies on general background knowledge of team strength that may be outdated for 2026.
Rosters, coaching changes, and QB situations for 2026 are not supplied.
